text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a slow creep of NCCL allreduce timeouts in us-west4 after the NCCL 2.28.1 push overnight. First spike ~01:10 UTC, now ~1.2% of inference requests hit an allreduce timeout and trigger retries. Multi-GPU A100 jobs mostly, seq len ~1024, continuous batching.

kevin: How big is the affected population? Canary failure or rollout-wide?

maria: Roughly 120 inference pods across ~30 nodes are showing increased timeouts. Canary was small (6 nodes) and looked OK at 22:00, widened at 00:30. Canary traces show occasional 40–60ms stalls that eventually escalate to the 5s NCCL timeout.

ops-bot: deploy log: rollout started by @deploy-bot 00:32 UTC — runtime:v3.7.1, nccl:2.28.1, driver:535.86.10

nina: Pasting a short trace snippet from one host (sanitized):
```
[01:09:58] allgather step 3 -> 94ms
[01:09:59] p2p stall detected on gpu0 -> 120ms
[01:10:03] nccl timeout triggered (5000ms) -> job retry
```

sam: Any signs of RDMA or NIC resets? I saw some cloud NIC flaps in metrics around 00:58. Could be coincidental.

maria: Kernel logs show sporadic dma_map/unmap WARNs on two nodes, but cloud NIC metrics don't show hard resets. Not universal across all impacted nodes.

kevin: Are these mixed GPU SKUs (A100 + A10) or homogeneous? Topology sometimes changes collective behavior.

maria: Yes — a few nodes are mixed (A100 + A10) because of a packing experiment last month. Those nodes have a higher failure rate.

nina: Two mitigation options: 1) pin the region back to NCCL 2.27.3; or 2) enable a runtime fallback to avoid P2P paths that might be tripping (NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 / NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SHM). The fallback will reduce perf.

sam: Disabling p2p will hit perf hard — rough estimate +25% token cost for hot workloads. Reverting NCCL is safer for customer SLAs.

kevin: Stop the rollout expansion. Do not widen to other regions until we have a root cause.

maria: Agreed. Proposed rollback plan: pin us-west4 to runtime:v3.7.0-nccl2.27.3. Rollout strategy: 10% canary now, 50% in 15m if no alarms, full region in 1h if green. Collect per-route latency + allreduce failure counts during rollout. I'll open infra PR and trigger rollback.

ops-bot: rollback job queued by @maria — job_id=7892

deploy-bot: rollback started on 6 nodes (canary). Status: in-progress.

nina: Also kicking off an inventory/audit for driver/kernel mismatches — saw a couple nodes on driver 470.x while most are 535.86.10. That mismatch could expose a kernel/driver/NCCL interaction bug.

kevin: Good. If rollback doesn't improve things, we need to capture per-GPU PCI topology + nvlink health + NCCL traces and escalate to vendor.

maria: Commands I'm running for trace collection (run on affected node):
```bash
sudo /opt/runtime/bin/collect_nccl_traces --since 1995000000 --out /tmp/nccl-trace.tgz
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference -o wide
ssh gpu-node-23 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-node-23.txt
```

sam: Also check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and /var/log/messages; grep for "nvlink" and "dma_map"

maria: Pinging support and customer success to prep for potential customer impact notifications. Preparing a short incident note and list of top affected tenants.

kevin: If rollback looks clean, schedule a cautious re-test: NCCL 2.28.1 -> subset of homogeneous A100 nodes only with full nvlink topologies, and run collective microbench for 12h.

nina: Inventory job started (node-driver-kernel-map). Will post CSV link when ready: https://internal.redwood/inventory/nwk-1995.csv

maria: For postmortem: capture the exact sequence (canary metrics at 22:00, widen at 00:30, first user errors at 01:10), list mitigations, and include cost delta for reverting vs degraded fallback.

kevin: If we must keep 2.28.x for some reason, we should add automatic regional fallback to a pinned nccl variant in the smart router to avoid full client impact. But let's focus on rollback first.

ops-bot: rollback canary reports: 4/6 nodes updated, monitoring metrics streaming to dashboard https://dashboard.redwood/orgs/infra/rollouts/7892

deploy-bot: rollback finished on canary nodes. Health checks: per-route error rate down from 1.2% -> 0.15% on canary.

maria: Canary looks promising. Proceeding to 50% per plan. Will post final status in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin: Thanks all. If this remains noisy after full rollback, open an expedited support ticket with NCCL/NVIDIA and prepare kernel+driver reproducible case.

maria: Noted. I'll follow up with a concise incident summary when the region is stable. :white_check_mark:
